notes.decision: Greek προγνώστης 'foreknower' (one who knows in advance). The Coptic spelling has ⲣⲛ for ⲅⲛ (assimilation/dialectal). Translated 'foreknower' to preserve the verbal-prefixed sense ('first-knower') which the chapter explicitly explicates in line 33-34 with ⲣ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲣⲉϩⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ 'first-know.' Avoided generic 'prophet' which loses the morpheme structure.

Reads as a Lycopolitan reduplicated/extended form of ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp, seize, hold,' parallel to the simpler ⲙⲁϩⲣ̄ in line 24 of the chapter heading. Translated 'grasp them' to match the heading's identical verb. The reduplication may intensify ('firmly grasp / take possession of').

Greek κατά + Lycopolitan ⲣⲁⲓ̈ (1sg suffix on prepositional ⲣⲁ⸗) = 'according to me / as I see it.' The elect is offering his interpretive perspective to the apostle, asking the question while proposing his own understanding of how the Mind of Light's grasp works. Standard Coptic 'κατὰ + suffix' construction.

Translated 'would be established for them.' ⲛⲉⲕⲏⲧ analyzed as past-irrealis copula ⲛⲉ- + qualitative ⲕⲏⲧ ('built/established,' qualitative of ⲕⲱⲧ); ⲛⲟⲛⲧⲟⲩ = ⲛ̄- + bound ⲟⲛⲧⲟⲩ ('to them, for them'). The clause functions as the apodosis of the implicit conditional that runs through the reason: 'a great toil WOULD be established for them, were they to know each other's hearts.'

Translated 'is fitting for him.' The lexeme ⲭⲙ̄ⲙⲉ is unattested in our glossary; reading as a Lycopolitan substantival relative meaning 'what pertains/befits.' Could alternatively reflect ϣⲙⲙⲟ (be a stranger/be foreign), ϣⲙ̄ϣⲉ (serve), or ϫⲱⲙ (yield). The contextual sense — that the Apostle as Mind is by nature one to whom every matter is revealed — strongly favors a 'fittingness/property' reading.

Translated 'and not be far from the path of his fellow.' ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ-ⲧⲙ̄- = negative conjunctive 'and not'; ⲟⲩⲉ = 'be far' (= Sah. ⲟⲩⲏⲩ); ⲫⲃⲓ̈ⲁϩ obscure — tentatively read as 'the path/manner/track' (possibly Lyc. variant of a journey/footstep noun). The sense of the line is that the Apostle's distinctive prophetic priority would be erased — the elect would become indistinguishable apostles, no further from each other than fellow-travellers on a single path.

Translated 'they would be sufficient unto (one another).' Tentatively analyzed as Greek loanword ἱκανός 'sufficient' verbalized with prefix ⲁⲥⲓ-/ⲣ̄- + ϩⲓⲕⲁⲛⲉ; cf. ⲡⲍⲓⲕⲁⲛⲟⲥ 'the able one' already in accumulated vocabulary. The second reason envisions the negative consequence that mutual heart-knowledge would erase the necessary differentiation among the elect, rendering each one merely the mirror-sufficient counterpart of the other.
Translated 'which they wear' (3pl-feminine direct object). ⲣ̄- + ⲫⲟⲣⲉ (Greek φορεῖν) = 'wear' (cf. ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲥ 'to bear/wear' in glossary); 3sg.f object suffix -ⲁⲥ refers back to ⲧⲥⲁⲣⲝ̄ 'the flesh.'

Translated 'send their light far forth.' Read as ⲣ̄- (do/make) + ⲡⲉⲟⲩⲉ ('the distance/being-far,' from ⲟⲩⲉ 'be far') + ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲟⲓⲛⲉ ('of their light') + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('forth') = 'cause their light to go far forth.' Captures the soteriological-spatial register of the Mind's outward-sending light, paralleling the contrast with 'gazing into righteousness' (line 28) versus '(falling) downward to the world' (line 29).

Translated 'labor' as Lyc reduction of ⲣ̄-ϩⲓⲥⲉ 'do toil/labor.' Context (alongside wage-laborers in the world to receive money) requires a labor-verb. Alternative reading as Lyc form of ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'be vigilant/watchful' is possible but contextually less apt.

Tentative 'wage-laborers'; agent-noun ⲣⲉϩ-/ⲣⲉϥ- + unidentified ⲕⲗⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ. Possibly Greek-derived (κλωνεύω 'turn,' κλόνος 'tumult,' or κοινωνός 'partner'). The context of going-around-for-wages suggests itinerant workers/laborers.

Read as Lycopolitan negative habitual 3pl/impersonal 'they do not give / it is not given,' with ⲙⲁϩ- corresponding to Sahidic ⲙⲉⲩ-. The clause 'this is therefore why no apocalypse is given to the elect' fits the contrastive logic with line 5 'but the matter is hidden from them indeed until...'
